subject: maths
title: Multiplying and Dividing with Groups
seo_title: Year 2 Multiplying and Dividing Worksheets: Equal Groups, Arrays, Sharing and Grouping (Free)
standard_text: Multiply and divide by one-digit numbers using repeated addition, equal grouping, arrays, and partitioning to support a variety of calculation strategies
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on multiplying and dividing, following the Australian Curriculum (AC9M2N05): equal groups and repeated addition, arrays, sharing equally, grouping and word problems. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: Multiplying is adding equal groups. Dividing is sharing equally or making equal groups.
key_sub: 3 groups of 4 = 4 + 4 + 4 = 3 × 4 = 12. 12 shared between 3 is 4 each, and 12 in groups of 3 is 4 groups: 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
body_html:
Equal groups

Multiplying is about equal groups. Count the groups. Count how many are in one group. Then add the same number again and again. This is repeated addition.

Example

There are 5 bags. Each bag has 2 apples. How many apples?

5 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. So 5 × 2 = 10.

Answer: 10 apples

Arrays

An array is objects in rows and columns. Rows go across. Columns go up and down. Count the rows or count the columns. You get the same total, so one array gives two number sentences.

You can also split an array into parts you know. 4 rows of 5 is 2 rows of 5 and 2 more rows of 5: 10 + 10 = 20.

Sharing equally

Dividing (÷) can mean sharing. You know how many plates. Give out one at a time until none are left. Every plate must get the same.

Grouping

Dividing can also mean grouping. You know how many go in each group. Make groups until none are left. Count the groups. Jumps on a number line work the same way.

Example

30 students make teams of 5. How many teams?

This is grouping. Count by 5s to 30: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 fives. 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

Answer: 6 teams

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the two numbers: 3 × 4 = 7Add 4 once for each group: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12
Counting the groups, not the objects: 3 groups of 4 = 3Count everything inside the rings: 12
Unequal groups: 12 shared as 5, 4 and 3Every share must be the same: 4, 4 and 4
Mixing up sharing and grouping: 10 in groups of 2 drawn as 2 groups of 5Groups of 2 means 2 in every group. That makes 5 groups

faq.q: What multiplication and division do Year 2 students learn in Australia?
faq.a: Year 2 students learn what multiplying and dividing mean. They use equal groups, repeated addition, arrays, sharing and grouping, mostly with groups of 2, 3, 5 and 10. Quick recall of multiplication facts for 3, 4, 5 and 10 comes in Year 3.

faq.q: What is the difference between sharing and grouping?
faq.a: In sharing, you know how many groups there are and find how many go in each (12 shared between 3 is 4 each). In grouping, you know how many go in each group and find how many groups (12 in groups of 3 is 4 groups). Both are 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

faq.q: How do arrays help Year 2 students with multiplication?
faq.a: An array shows equal rows, so students can count by 2s, 5s or 10s instead of counting one by one. It also shows that 2 × 5 and 5 × 2 give the same total, and a big array can be split into smaller parts.

faq.q: How do you explain multiplication to a Year 2 child?
faq.a: Start with equal groups of real objects, such as 3 plates of 4 biscuits. Add the groups (4 + 4 + 4 = 12), then show that 3 × 4 = 12 is a short way to write it.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: there are 3 groups. 2 is how many counters are in each group.
Count the rings: there are 4 groups. 5 is how many stars are in each group.

items.q: How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: there are 5 groups. 3 is how many blocks are in each group.

items.q: How many counters are in each group?
items.e: Look inside one ring. It has 5 counters. Every group is the same.
Look inside one ring. It has 2 stars. Every group is the same.

items.q: How many blocks are in each group?
items.e: Look inside one ring. It has 3 blocks. Every group is the same.

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: 2 groups of 3. Count by 3s: 3, 6. There are 6. (Not 2 + 3 = 5: that adds the number of groups to the number in one group.)
5 groups of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. There are 10. (Not 5 + 2 = 7: that adds the number of groups to the number in one group.)

items.q: How many blocks are there altogether?
items.e: 3 groups of 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15. There are 15. (Not 3 + 5 = 8: that adds the number of groups to the number in one group.)

items.q: How many counters are there altogether?
items.e: 2 groups of 10. Count by 10s: 10, 20. There are 20. (Not 2 + 10 = 12: that adds the number of groups to the number in one group.)
There are 3 groups. Each group has 5. Add 5, 3 times: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: Which addition matches the picture?
items.e: There are 4 groups. Each group has 2. Add 2, 4 times: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8.
There are 3 groups. Each group has 10. Add 10, 3 times: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30.
4 groups of 5 is written 4 × 5. It means 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: 3 groups of 2 is written 3 × 2. It means 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: 5 groups of 5 is written 5 × 5. It means 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 25.

items.q: Which picture shows 3 groups of 4?
items.e: B has 3 rings with 4 counters in each. Check both numbers: count the groups, then count inside one group. All the groups must be equal.
B has 2 rings with 5 stars in each. Check both numbers: count the groups, then count inside one group. All the groups must be equal.

items.q: Which picture shows 5 groups of 2?
items.e: C has 5 rings with 2 blocks in each. Check both numbers: count the groups, then count inside one group. All the groups must be equal.

items.q: Which is the same as 3 groups of 5?
items.e: 3 groups of 5 means 5, three times: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15. It is also 3 × 5.

items.q: How many rows are in this array?
items.e: Rows go across. Count from top to bottom: 3 rows. Each row has 5.
Columns go up and down. Count from left to right: 4 columns. Each column has 2.

items.q: How many blocks are in the array?
items.e: 2 rows of 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10. That is 10. It is 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: How many counters are in the array?
items.e: 4 rows of 2. Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 8. It is 4 × 2 = 8.
3 rows of 10. Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30. That is 30. It is 3 × 10 = 30.

items.q: How many blocks are in the array?
items.e: 5 rows of 5. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 25. It is 5 × 5 = 25.

items.q: Which two number sentences match this array?
items.e: Rows: 2 rows of 3 is 2 × 3. Columns: 3 columns of 2 is 3 × 2. Both make 6, so both match.
Rows: 4 rows of 5 is 4 × 5. Columns: 5 columns of 4 is 5 × 4. Both make 20, so both match.
Rows: 5 rows of 10 is 5 × 10. Columns: 10 columns of 5 is 10 × 5. Both make 50, so both match.

items.q: This array shows 2 × 10 = 20. Which other number sentence does it show?
items.e: Count the columns: 10 columns of 2. That is 10 × 2 = 20. The rows give 2 × 10 = 20. Same array, same total.

items.q: This array shows 5 × 3 = 15. Which other number sentence does it show?
items.e: Count the columns: 3 columns of 5. That is 3 × 5 = 15. The rows give 5 × 3 = 15. Same array, same total.
Count the columns: 4 columns of 3. That is 4 × 3 = 12. The rows give 3 × 4 = 12. Same array, same total.

items.q: The array is split into two parts. How many counters are there in all?
items.e: Top part: 2 × 5 = 10. Bottom part: 2 × 5 = 10. Add the parts: 10 + 10 = 20. That is 4 × 5 = 20.

items.q: The array is split into two parts. How many counters are there in all?
items.e: Top part: 2 × 3 = 6. Bottom part: 3 × 3 = 9. Add the parts: 6 + 9 = 15. That is 5 × 3 = 15.
Top part: 2 × 10 = 20. Bottom part: 2 × 10 = 20. Add the parts: 20 + 20 = 40. That is 4 × 10 = 40.
You can multiply in any order. 5 × 2 and 2 × 5 are the same array turned around. So 2 × 5 = 10 too.
You can multiply in any order. 10 × 3 and 3 × 10 are the same array turned around. So 3 × 10 = 30 too.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 3 × 10 = 30 and 10 × 3 = 30. You can swap the numbers in a multiplication: 3 × 10 = 10 × 3.

items.q: Ruby says 2 × 5 and 5 × 2 have different answers. Is she right?
items.e: 2 fives make 10, and 5 twos make 10. No. Both are 10. The order does not matter in ×.

items.q: Which one is not true?
items.e: 5 × 3 = 15, but 5 + 3 = 8. So 5 × 3 = 5 + 3 is not true. The others just swap the order, and that is fine in ×.

items.q: Share these 10 counters equally between 2 plates. How many does each plate get?
items.e: Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each plate gets 5. 10 ÷ 2 = 5.
Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each plate gets 2. 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

items.q: Share these 15 counters equally between 5 plates. How many does each plate get?
items.e: Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each plate gets 3. 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

items.q: Share these 20 blocks equally between 2 bags. How many does each bag get?
items.e: Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each bag gets 10. 20 ÷ 2 = 10.
Give out one at a time, round and round, until none are left. Each bag gets 10. 30 ÷ 3 = 10.

items.q: 12 counters are shared between 3 plates. Which number sentence matches?
items.e: 12 counters are shared between 3 plates. Each plate has 4. That is 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

items.q: 10 counters are shared between 5 plates. Which number sentence matches?
items.e: 10 counters are shared between 5 plates. Each plate has 2. That is 10 ÷ 5 = 2.
20 counters are shared between 2 plates. Each plate has 10. That is 20 ÷ 2 = 10.

items.q: 15 counters are shared between 3 plates. Which number sentence matches?
items.e: 15 counters are shared between 3 plates. Each plate has 5. That is 15 ÷ 3 = 5.

items.q: Share 12 counters equally between 4 plates. Which picture shows this?
items.e: Sharing between 4 plates means 4 plates, all the same. A has 4 plates of 3. 3 plates of 4 is the wrong number of plates. 3, 3, 3 and 2 is not equal.
Sharing between 2 plates means 2 plates with the same amount. B has 5 and 5. 6 and 4 is not fair. 5 plates of 2 is the wrong number of plates.

items.q: Oliver wants to share 10 counters equally between 2 plates. How many counters must move?
items.e: 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so each plate needs 5. Move 1 from the 6 to the 4: 5 and 5. (Moving 2 would just swap the plates around.)

items.q: Liam wants to share 10 counters equally between 2 plates. How many counters must move?
items.e: 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so each plate needs 5. Move 2 from the 7 to the 3: 5 and 5. (Moving 4 would just swap the plates around.)

items.q: Share 16 counters equally between 2 friends. How many does each friend get?
items.e: Share out 2 at a time, or count by 2s to 16: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. That is 8 twos, so each gets 8. 16 ÷ 2 = 8.

items.q: Share 25 counters equally between 5 friends. How many does each friend get?
items.e: Share out 5 at a time, or count by 5s to 25: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. That is 5 fives, so each gets 5. 25 ÷ 5 = 5.

items.q: Share 40 counters equally between 10 friends. How many does each friend get?
items.e: Share out 10 at a time, or count by 10s to 40: 10, 20, 30, 40. That is 4 tens, so each gets 4. 40 ÷ 10 = 4.

items.q: Which shows 10 shared equally between 2?
items.e: Equal shares are the same size. 5 + 5 = 10 and both are 5, so 5 and 5. 6 and 4 also make 10, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which number sentence shows 15 shared between 5?
items.e: Sharing is division. Start with the amount you share: 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Each gets 3.

items.q: William shared 12 counters between 3 plates. What went wrong?
c: The plates are not equal. Each should have 4.
items.e: The total is right, but equal shares must be the same. 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so each plate should have 4.

items.q: 20 shared between 5 is 4 each. Which number sentence checks this?
items.e: 5 friends with 4 each: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 20. So 4 × 5 = 20 checks the sharing.
Count the rings: 3 groups. 15 in groups of 5 makes 3 groups, so 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

items.q: 8 counters are put into groups of 2. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: 4 groups. 8 in groups of 2 makes 4 groups, so 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

items.q: 30 blocks are put into groups of 10. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: 3 groups. 30 in groups of 10 makes 3 groups, so 30 ÷ 10 = 3.

items.q: 9 counters are put into groups of 3. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count the rings: 3 groups. 9 in groups of 3 makes 3 groups, so 9 ÷ 3 = 3.
Circle 5 at a time until none are left. Or count by 5s to 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 groups. 20 ÷ 5 = 4.
Circle 2 at a time until none are left. Or count by 2s to 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 groups. 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

items.q: How many groups of 10 can you make with these 40 blocks?
items.e: Circle 10 at a time until none are left. Or count by 10s to 40: 10, 20, 30, 40. That is 4 groups. 40 ÷ 10 = 4.

items.q: How many jumps of 2 does it take to get from 0 to 10?
items.e: Count the jumps: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. There are 5 jumps of 2. So 10 ÷ 2 = 5.

items.q: How many jumps of 5 does it take to get from 0 to 25?
items.e: Count the jumps: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. There are 5 jumps of 5. So 25 ÷ 5 = 5.

items.q: How many jumps of 3 does it take to get from 0 to 18?
items.e: Count the jumps: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. There are 6 jumps of 3. So 18 ÷ 3 = 6.

items.q: There are 40 counters. Put them in groups of 10. How many groups?
items.e: Count by 10s until you reach 40: 10, 20, 30, 40. That is 4 groups. 40 ÷ 10 = 4.

items.q: There are 35 counters. Put them in groups of 5. How many groups?
items.e: Count by 5s until you reach 35: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. That is 7 groups. 35 ÷ 5 = 7.

items.q: There are 14 counters. Put them in groups of 2. How many groups?
items.e: Count by 2s until you reach 14: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. That is 7 groups. 14 ÷ 2 = 7.

items.q: Grace has 10 lollies. She puts 2 lollies in each bag. Which picture shows this?
items.e: She puts 2 lollies in each bag, so every bag has 2. A has 5 bags of 2. 2 bags of 5 is sharing between 2, not groups of 2.

items.q: Put 15 blocks into groups of 3. Which picture shows this?
items.e: Groups of 3 means 3 in every ring. A has 5 rings of 3, which is 15. 3 rings of 5 is groups of 5. 4 rings of 3 is only 12.

items.q: Which one is grouping?
items.e: Grouping means you know how many go in each group. “Boxes of 2” tells you 2 in each box: Put 10 eggs in boxes of 2. That makes 5 boxes. Sharing between 2 boxes gives 5 in each box.

items.q: 12 counters are put into groups of 3. Which number sentence matches?
items.e: 12 counters in groups of 3 make 4 groups. Start with the whole amount: 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

items.q: 10 counters are put into groups of 5. Which number sentence matches?
items.e: 10 counters in groups of 5 make 2 groups. Start with the whole amount: 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

items.q: Noah shares 15 counters between 5 friends. His friend puts 15 counters in groups of 5. What number do they both get?
items.e: Sharing: 15 shared between 5 is 3 each. Grouping: 15 in groups of 5 is 3 groups. Both are 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

items.q: How many groups of 10 are in 60?

items.e: 3 groups of 10: 10, 20, 30. 3 × 10 = 30 strawberries.

items.q: A kookaburra has 2 legs. There are 6 kookaburras on a branch. How many legs is that?
A wombat has 4 legs. There are 3 wombats. How many legs is that?
items.e: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. 3 × 4 = 12 legs. (3 + 4 = 7 adds the wombats to the legs.)

items.q: At the sausage sizzle, each tray has 5 sausages. There are 4 trays. How many sausages is that?
An ice block costs $2 at the canteen. Chloe buys 5 ice blocks. How much does she pay?
Zara has seven 10c coins. How much money is that?
Chairs are set out in 3 rows of 5 for assembly. How many chairs is that?
20 students make 2 equal teams for footy. How many students are in each team?
items.e: 20 shared between 2 teams: 20 ÷ 2 = 10. Check: 10 + 10 = 20.

items.q: 30 students make groups of 5 for sport. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count by 5s to 30: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 fives. 30 ÷ 5 = 6 groups.

items.q: A baker has 18 muffins. She puts 2 muffins in each box. How many boxes does she fill?
items.e: 18 in groups of 2: count by 2s to 18 and you say 9 numbers. 18 ÷ 2 = 9 boxes.

items.q: A teacher has 40 pencils. She puts 10 in each tub. How many tubs does she need?
Share 14 crackers equally between 2 plates. How many crackers go on each plate?
items.e: Half of 14 is 7. 14 ÷ 2 = 7 crackers. Check: 7 + 7 = 14.

items.q: Ava has 50c in 10c coins. How many coins does she have?
items.e: 10c, 20c, 30c, 40c, 50c. That is 5 coins. 50 ÷ 10 = 5 coins.

items.q: Some kookaburras sit on a fence. They have 10 legs altogether. Each one has 2 legs. How many kookaburras are there?
items.e: 10 legs in groups of 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. 10 ÷ 2 = 5 kookaburras. (20 is 10 × 2, the wrong way.)

items.q: There are 35 crayons. 5 crayons fit in each box. How many boxes are needed?
items.e: 35 ÷ 5: count by 5s to 35. That is 7 fives. 7 boxes.

items.q: Amelia has 3 bags of 10 marbles. She gives away 5 marbles. How many marbles are left?
items.e: Step 1: 3 × 10 = 30. Step 2: 30 − 5 = 25 marbles.

items.q: Mia has 2 cartons of 5 eggs. She uses 3 eggs. How many eggs are left?
items.e: Step 1: 2 × 5 = 10 eggs. Step 2: 10 − 3 = 7 eggs. (4 comes from 2 + 5 − 3.)

items.q: There are 15 apples. They are put into bags of 5. Which number sentence tells you how many bags?
items.e: Putting into bags of 5 is grouping, so divide: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 bags.

items.q: Jack says, “I have 3 bags of 4 marbles. That is 7 marbles.” What went wrong?
c: He counted the bags. It is 3.
items.e: 3 + 4 = 7 adds the bags to one bag. 3 bags of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4. He added. It is 3 × 4 = 12.
